name: Program in Cell and Molecular Biology (CMB)
summary: Interdisciplinary PhD program at Duke, run with the Department of Cell Biology. Students do research in three or more labs of their choice before selecting an advisor.

deadlines.label: Application deadline
deadlines.note: The Graduate School lists 12/01/2026 for fall 2027 entry, at 11:59:59 p.m. Eastern. The CMB admissions page still refers to Fall 2026 admission.

timeline.interviews: Selected applicants are invited to interview online with faculty and current students. The program page still shows last season's recruitment date (February 19–21, 2026).

english.note: If your first language isn't English. These are the Graduate School's usual minimums; admitted students average higher. Duolingo reports must include subscores. For Fall 2027, scores must be dated August 1, 2024 or later. Waived after two years of full-time study at a college where English is the only language of instruction, in a country where English is the main spoken language. Admitted international students take English placement exams on arrival.

applicationFee.note: Graduate School waivers are for US citizens and permanent residents who meet its conditions, first come, first served. The CMB page says fee waivers aren't available to international applicants.

requirements.note: Review is holistic: research and other experience, writing and communication, persistence and motivation, and coursework and GPA. No writing sample is needed, and CMB doesn't review video essays.

funding.note: All PhD students in their five-year guaranteed funding period receive 12-month stipends, with tuition, fees and health insurance premiums covered. First-year CMB students are supported by Graduate School fellowships; after that, by their mentor's research grants, teaching assistantships or outside fellowships.
